On 10/18/2026 11:03 AM, Chloe Martin wrote:
> I sketched a preliminary reference diagram that follows our usual private deployment pattern...

Nice start. A few hands-on notes from infra:

1) Control plane placement
- Strong preference: customer-managed control plane endpoint (hosted in their VPC) that speaks to our management plane over mTLS on a known port. This avoids inbound firewall exceptions on Redwood side.
- Alternative: a lightweight control plane sidecar inside their subnet that syncs with our management plane via an outbound-only websocket tunnel (if they insist on no public endpoints). That has higher ops overhead and complicates upgrades.

2) Data plane egress pattern
- Recommend a two-tier egress: (a) model fetches and artifact pulls use a presigned S3 path through their internal proxy; (b) telemetry and usage metrics forwarded to our metrics collector via a dedicated egress proxy with redact rules applied.
- Clarify whether Helios requires local KV stores for cache — we can run ephemeral local cache on data plane hosts with periodic encrypted snapshot to their object store.

3) Ports/CIDR
- Minimal list: outbound 443 to redwood-mgmt.redwood-internal.com, outbound 443 to prometheus/metrics endpoints (if enabled), ephemeral ports for internode (configurable, default 61000-61999).

I've attached a quick notes file with recommended defaults and a short checklist for the runbook.

Attachment: controlplane-placement-notes.txt (TXT, 6KB)

I'll be on the Tue 10am slot.

-Jonas
Senior Infrastructure Engineer

Date: 2026-10-21T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final: private network schematic + ops handoff (meeting notes and runbook draft)

Mike — thanks for the sync today. Quick summary and next steps so Helios has a single source of truth: 

Decisions and assumptions
- Control plane: customer-hosted endpoint inside Helios VPC (TLS terminated by Helios). We will use mTLS from Redwood control components for authenticated management calls.
- Data plane: runs in a dedicated subnet with ephemeral local cache; artifacts pulled from Helios object store using presigned URLs.
- Egress and telemetry: Redwood will forward telemetry to Helios egress proxy; we will apply redact rules (no raw prompt payloads). Full request-level logs will be kept in Helios account if they opt-in.

Handoff items for Helios
- Provide control-plane FQDN and cert (wildcard or SAN) + preferred KMS ARN for artifact encryption
- Firewall: allow outbound 443 to redwood-mgmt.redwood-internal.com and allow the ephemeral inter-node port range if they choose to enable inter-host health checks
- Confirm retention window for audit logs (default 90 days)

Attached: private-deploy-runbook-v0.1.md (MD, 18KB) — contains checklist, runbook steps for failover, and the final annotated schematic we agreed on in the call. Also attached the notes Jonas circulated. I've added a short rollout plan (canary with one tenant followed by 50% rollout).

Next steps
- Helios to confirm FQDN and KMS choice by 2026-10-25
- Redwood ops will produce an automated deployment manifest and a CNM (configuration) snippet for Helios' infra team by 2026-10-27
- Follow-up post-deploy smoke test runbook will be shared and scheduled for the week after deploy.

If Helios wants the lightweight control-plane sidecar pattern instead, we documented tradeoffs in the runbook. Otherwise we'll proceed with the customer-hosted control plane approach.

Thanks all — Chloe
Product Operations, Redwood Inference
